title: Protocol and Deadline
premise: Coral Villalobos built his life on being unattributable: an interpreter who translates for delegations doomed to fail and takes the cases no agency will claim. When a stranger repays a favor Coral never performed—and demands interest—he learns he was never freelance at all; he is an asset of Meridian, the deniable training network that shaped him, and his 'debt' is a mission to destroy it from inside. As Coral burns safehouses, handlers, and finally the archive that holds his own recruitment file, he must decide whether survival means erasing what he was or owning it. The book ends with Coral handing the archive to a journalist and walking into a Geneva hearing as a named witness—visible at last, and hunted for it.
about_author: Sable Winterbourne is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where the real agreements were never the ones on the table. They write thrillers about people whose professions require them to have no biography.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In a failing Geneva backchannel, Coral interprets a ceasefire he knows is theater, then finds a stranger waiting in his apartment who thanks him for a rescue in Sarajevo—a rescue Coral has no memory of performing. The beat: unease dressed as politeness.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The stranger, Anselm, leaves a ledger page listing Coral's aliases and a deadline: fourteen days to open a door inside Meridian's Zurich office or the debt is collected from Coral's sister. Beat: the floor drops out of his invisibility.

chapters.title: Consecutive Lies
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral tests whether Anselm's dossier is authentic by running a trap through an old contact, Ilsa, who confirms one alias too many—the kind only Meridian itself would know. Beat: cold recognition that his handler may be his blackmailer.

chapters.title: Delegation of One
chapters.summary: POV Mara Okonkwo, a delegation aide who notices Coral passing notes no interpreter should carry. She covers for him without knowing why, and the two form a wary alliance. Beat: the first warmth in a story of transactions.

chapters.title: Zurich, After Hours
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Using a dead colleague's credentials, Coral enters Meridian's front company and finds the archive vault—but also a kill list with tomorrow's date, and his own name third from the top. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Training Was For
chapters.summary: POV Coral, flashback-woven. Interrogating his own memory, Coral reconstructs how Meridian recruited him after Sarajevo: not saved by a stranger, but harvested. Beat: grief for the self he was before the network.

chapters.title: The Kill List
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Revealed: Anselm is a Meridian cleaner ordered to burn loose assets, and Coral is both target and tool—an experiment in turning an asset against its maker. Beat: villainy with a professional's calm.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral moves his sister Lena to safety and trades a minor Meridian secret to Ilsa for vault schematics, burning a bridge he'll need later. Beat: the price of survival paid in installments.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At the peace talks' collapse, Mara catches Coral feeding disinformation to both sides and confronts him; he tells her enough truth to recruit her instead of lose her. Beat: trust gambled deliberately.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. First attempt on the archive fails—Meridian anticipated him, because they wrote his methods. He escapes by doing something untrained: surrendering control to Mara's plan. Beat: humiliation transmuted into adaptation.

chapters.title: Handlers All the Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Anselm reports to Director Voss, who reveals the deeper game: the peace delegation's failure is engineered to justify Meridian's expansion. Beat: scale of corruption revealed.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Diplomacy
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral leaks a fragment of the kill list to force Meridian to reshuffle, flushing three hidden handlers into the open; two flee, one dies messily. Beat: power tasted, and found addictive.

chapters.title: Lena's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Coral's sister, no passive victim, decodes the ledger page Anselm left and finds the favor-that-never-happened was her rescue—Coral took the fall for her years ago. Beat: family debt inverted.

chapters.title: The Middleman's Price
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral turns a captured handler, who gives up Voss's location but warns that the archive is booby-trapped with a data-destroying failsafe keyed to Coral's biometrics. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Interpreting Voss
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A staged meeting: Voss offers Coral partnership, arguing Meridian's order prevents worse chaos, and Coral genuinely wavers. Beat: temptation articulated better than any threat.

chapters.title: What Mara Saw
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Following Coral after the Voss meeting, Mara finds evidence he may have accepted—and prepares to expose him if he did. Beat: alliance strained to breaking.

chapters.title: Fourteen Days, Spent
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Deadline eve. Coral sets the final con: fake his own death on the kill list while Mara triggers the failsafe remotely, forcing Meridian to choose between exposing the archive or losing it. Beat: controlled fury.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns Twice
chapters.summary: POV Coral and Mara alternating. The vault operation half-succeeds: the failsafe destroys Meridian's copies, but Coral secretly preserves the core files—including his own recruitment record. Beat: triumph shadowed by choice.

chapters.title: Anselm's Last Assignment
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Ordered to kill Coral regardless, Anselm hesitates—Coral spares him once, mirroring the favor motif—and defects with proof of Voss's engineered summit collapse. Beat: the instrument developing a conscience.

chapters.title: Voss Descending
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Climax: confrontation with Voss aboard a departing diplomatic train; Coral defeats her not with violence but by broadcasting the archive live, making her power worthless in front of witnesses. Beat: exposure as weapon.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Aftermath: Meridian dismantled publicly, but Coral must testify under his true name, surrendering every alias. Lena watches; Mara stands beside him. Beat: the terror and relief of being seen.

chapters.title: Protocol, Revised
chapters.summary: POV Coral, months later. Working openly now as a translator for tribunals, Coral receives another stranger's envelope—a new network stirring—and smiles, because this time he knows exactly who he is. Beat: sequel-ready resolve without erasing cost.
